verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev claims elastic, managed auto-scaling with nothing to provision and says it processes millions of tasks. Throughput is raised through queue concurrency limits and purchasable extra concurrency, and checkpoint-resume plus retries give some resilience; users report scaling effortlessly. However, the evidence never documents adding workers to a fleet, load-balancing across workers, or explicit tolerance of worker loss. Missing for 10: documented worker-fleet horizontal scaling (e.g. for self-hosted), load-balancing semantics across workers, explicit worker-failure/run-reassignment behavior, independent scale benchmarks.
